content.title: About
content.content: Steel‑cut whole grain oats are whole oat kernels that have been chopped into small pieces. They retain the bran and germ, making them high in fiber, vitamins, and minerals. When cooked they form a thick, creamy porridge with a subtle nutty flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Steel‑cut processing is one of the oldest methods of oat preparation, using only mechanical cracking.
Unlike instant oats, steel‑cut oats require a longer cooking time (about 20‑30 minutes).
Oats are among the world’s oldest cultivated crops, grown for over 10,000 years.
They are a staple in traditional Scandinavian and Celtic dishes.
Steel‑cut oats retain more nutrients than extruded oat products.

items.title: Rich in beta‑glucan
items.content: Beta‑glucan is a soluble fiber that helps lower cholesterol and supports heart health.

items.title: Stabilizes blood sugar
items.content: Slow‑release carbohydrates help maintain steady glucose levels after meals.

items.title: Source of magnesium and phosphorus
items.content: These minerals are essential for muscle, nerve, and bone function.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Avenanthramides and phenolic compounds protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber promotes intestinal motility and a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Cereal allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to oats.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; soaking or sprouting lowers its level.

items.title: Gluten cross‑contamination
items.content: Oats are often processed on the same equipment as wheat; people with celiac disease should choose certified gluten‑free oats.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Steel‑cut oats can be boiled in water or milk, added to soups, stews, baked goods, and energy bars. Rinse them before cooking and, if desired, soak for 4‑6 hours to shorten cooking time.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For long‑term storage keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent the fats from becoming rancid.
